1.sahih_international: Nun. By the pen and what they inscribe,
1.pickthall: Nun. By the pen and that which they write (therewith),
1.yusuf_ali: Nun. By the Pen and the (Record) which (men) write,-
1.shakir: Noon. I swear by the pen and what the angels write,
1.muhammad_sarwar: Nun. By the pen and by what you write,
1.mohsin_khan: Nun. [These letters (Nun, etc.) are one of the miracles of the Quran, and none but Allah (Alone) knows their meanings]. By the pen and what the (angels) write (in the Records of men).
1.arberry: Nun. By the Pen, and what they inscribe,

2.sahih_international: You are not, [O Muhammad], by the favor of your Lord, a madman.
2.pickthall: Thou art not, for thy Lord's favour unto thee, a madman.
2.yusuf_ali: Thou art not, by the Grace of thy Lord, mad or possessed.
2.shakir: By the grace of your Lord you are not mad.
2.muhammad_sarwar: (Muhammad), you are not insane, thanks to the bounty of your Lord.
2.mohsin_khan: You (O Muhammad SAW) are not, by the Grace of your Lord, a madman.
2.arberry: thou art not, by the blessing of thy Lord, a man possessed.

3.sahih_international: And indeed, for you is a reward uninterrupted.
3.pickthall: And lo! thine verily will be a reward unfailing.
3.yusuf_ali: Nay, verily for thee is a Reward unfailing:
3.shakir: And most surely you shall have a reward never to be cut off.
3.muhammad_sarwar: You will certainly receive a never-ending reward.
3.mohsin_khan: And verily, for you (O Muhammad SAW) will be an endless reward.
3.arberry: Surely thou shalt have a wage unfailing;

4.sahih_international: And indeed, you are of a great moral character.
4.pickthall: And lo! thou art of a tremendous nature.
4.yusuf_ali: And thou (standest) on an exalted standard of character.
4.shakir: And most surely you conform (yourself) to sublime morality.
4.muhammad_sarwar: You have attained a high moral standard.
4.mohsin_khan: And verily, you (O Muhammad SAW) are on an exalted standard of character.
4.arberry: surely thou art upon a mighty morality.

5.sahih_international: So you will see and they will see
5.pickthall: And thou wilt see and they will see
5.yusuf_ali: Soon wilt thou see, and they will see,
5.shakir: So you shall see, and they (too) shall see,
5.muhammad_sarwar: You will see and they will also see
5.mohsin_khan: You will see, and they will see,
5.arberry: So thou shalt see, and they will see,

6.sahih_international: Which of you is the afflicted [by a devil].
6.pickthall: Which of you is the demented.
6.yusuf_ali: Which of you is afflicted with madness.
6.shakir: Which of you is afflicted with madness.
6.muhammad_sarwar: which of you has been afflicted by insanity.
6.mohsin_khan: Which of you is afflicted with madness.
6.arberry: which of you is the demented.

7.sahih_international: Indeed, your Lord is most knowing of who has gone astray from His way, and He is most knowing of the [rightly] guided.
7.pickthall: Lo! thy Lord is Best Aware of him who strayeth from His way, and He is Best Aware of those who walk aright.
7.yusuf_ali: Verily it is thy Lord that knoweth best, which (among men) hath strayed from His Path: and He knoweth best those who receive (true) Guidance.
7.shakir: Surely your Lord best knows him who errs from His way, and He best knows the followers of the right course.
7.muhammad_sarwar: Your Lord knows best who has gone astray from His path and who is rightly guided.
7.mohsin_khan: Verily, your Lord knows better, who (among men) has gone astray from His Path, and He knows better those who are guided.
7.arberry: Surely thy Lord knows very well those who have gone astray from His way, and He knows very well those who are guided.

8.sahih_international: Then do not obey the deniers.
8.pickthall: Therefor obey not thou the rejecters
8.yusuf_ali: So hearken not to those who deny (the Truth).
8.shakir: So do not yield to the rejecters.
8.muhammad_sarwar: Do not yield to those who reject the Truth.
8.mohsin_khan: So (O Muhammad SAW) obey not the deniers [(of Islamic Monotheism those who belie the Verses of Allah), the Oneness of Allah, and the Messenger of Allah (Muhammad SAW), etc.]
8.arberry: So obey thou not those who cry lies.

9.sahih_international: They wish that you would soften [in your position], so they would soften [toward you].
9.pickthall: Who would have had thee compromise, that they may compromise.
9.yusuf_ali: Their desire is that thou shouldst be pliant: so would they be pliant.
9.shakir: They wish that you should be pliant so they (too) would be pliant.
9.muhammad_sarwar: They would like you to relent to them so that they could also relent towards you.
9.mohsin_khan: They wish that you should compromise (in religion out of courtesy) with them, so they (too) would compromise with you.
9.arberry: They wish that thou shouldst compromise, then they would compromise.

10.sahih_international: And do not obey every worthless habitual swearer
10.pickthall: Neither obey thou each feeble oath-monger,
10.yusuf_ali: Heed not the type of despicable men,- ready with oaths,
10.shakir: And yield not to any mean swearer
10.muhammad_sarwar: Do not yield to one persistent in swearing,
10.mohsin_khan: And obey not everyone who swears much, and is considered worthless,
10.arberry: And obey thou not every mean swearer,

11.sahih_international: [And] scorner, going about with malicious gossip -
11.yusuf_ali: A slanderer, going about with calumnies,
11.mohsin_khan: A slanderer, going about with calumnies,

12.sahih_international: A preventer of good, transgressing and sinful,
12.pickthall: Hinderer of the good, transgressor, malefactor
12.yusuf_ali: (Habitually) hindering (all) good, transgressing beyond bounds, deep in sin,
12.shakir: Forbidder of good, outstepping the limits, sinful,
12.mohsin_khan: Hinderer of the good, transgressor, sinful,
12.arberry: hinderer of good, guilty aggressor, coarse-grained,

13.sahih_international: Cruel, moreover, and an illegitimate pretender.
13.yusuf_ali: Violent (and cruel),- with all that, base-born,-
13.muhammad_sarwar: ill-mannered, and moraly corrupt or that because he may possess wealth and children.
13.mohsin_khan: Cruel, after all that base-born (of illegitimate birth),

14.sahih_international: Because he is a possessor of wealth and children,
14.pickthall: It is because he is possessed of wealth and children
14.yusuf_ali: Because he possesses wealth and (numerous) sons.
14.shakir: Because he possesses wealth and sons.
14.muhammad_sarwar: When Our revelations are recited to him,
14.mohsin_khan: (He was so) because he had wealth and children.
14.arberry: because he has wealth and sons.

15.sahih_international: When Our verses are recited to him, he says, "Legends of the former peoples."
15.pickthall: That, when Our revelations are recited unto him, he saith: Mere fables of the men of old.
15.yusuf_ali: When to him are rehearsed Our Signs, "Tales of the ancients", he cries!
15.shakir: When Our communications are recited to him, he says: Stories of those of yore.
15.mohsin_khan: When Our Verses (of the Quran) are recited to him, he says: "Tales of the men of old!"
15.arberry: When Our signs are recited to him, he says, 'Fairy-tales of the ancients!'

16.sahih_international: We will brand him upon the snout.
16.pickthall: We shall brand him on the nose.
16.yusuf_ali: Soon shall We brand (the beast) on the snout!
16.shakir: We will brand him on the nose.
16.muhammad_sarwar: We shall brand him on his nose.
16.mohsin_khan: We shall brand him over the nose!
16.arberry: We shall brand him upon the muzzle!

17.sahih_international: Indeed, We have tried them as We tried the companions of the garden, when they swore to cut its fruit in the [early] morning
17.pickthall: Lo! We have tried them as We tried the owners of the garden when they vowed that they would pluck its fruit next morning,
17.yusuf_ali: Verily We have tried them as We tried the People of the Garden, when they resolved to gather the fruits of the (garden) in the morning.
17.shakir: Surely We will try them as We tried the owners of the garden, when they swore that they would certainly cut off the produce in the morning,
17.muhammad_sarwar: We have tested them in the same way as we tested the dwellers of the garden (in Yemen) when they swore to pluck all the fruits of the garden in the morning,
17.mohsin_khan: Verily, We have tried them as We tried the people of the garden, when they swore to pluck the fruits of the (garden) in the morning,
17.arberry: Now We have tried them, even as We tried the owners of the garden when they swore they would pluck in the morning

18.pickthall: And made no exception (for the Will of Allah);
18.yusuf_ali: But made no reservation, ("If it be Allah's Will").
18.shakir: And were not willing to set aside a portion (for the poor).
18.mohsin_khan: Without saying: Insha' Allah (If Allah will).
18.arberry: and they added not the saving words.

19.sahih_international: So there came upon the garden an affliction from your Lord while they were asleep.
19.pickthall: Then a visitation from thy Lord came upon it while they slept
19.yusuf_ali: Then there came on the (garden) a visitation from thy Lord, (which swept away) all around, while they were asleep.
19.shakir: Then there encompassed it a visitation from your Lord while they were sleeping.
19.muhammad_sarwar: A visitor from your Lord circled around the garden during the night while they were asleep
19.mohsin_khan: Then there passed by on the (garden) something (fire) from your Lord at night and burnt it while they were asleep.
19.arberry: Then a visitation from thy Lord visited it, while they were sleeping,

20.sahih_international: And it became as though reaped.
20.pickthall: And in the morning it was as if plucked.
20.yusuf_ali: So the (garden) became, by the morning, like a dark and desolate spot, (whose fruit had been gathered).
20.shakir: So it became as black, barren land.
20.muhammad_sarwar: and the garden was turned into a barren desert.
20.mohsin_khan: So the (garden) became black by the morning, like a pitch dark night (in complete ruins).
20.arberry: and in the morning it was as if it were a garden plucked.

21.sahih_international: And they called one another at morning,
21.pickthall: And they cried out one unto another in the morning,
21.yusuf_ali: As the morning broke, they called out, one to another,-
21.shakir: And they called out to each other in the morning,
21.muhammad_sarwar: In the morning they called out to one another,
21.mohsin_khan: Then they called out one to another as soon as the morning broke,
21.arberry: In the morning they called to one another,

22.sahih_international: [Saying], "Go early to your crop if you would cut the fruit."
22.pickthall: Saying: Run unto your field if ye would pluck (the fruit).
22.yusuf_ali: "Go ye to your tilth (betimes) in the morning, if ye would gather the fruits."
22.shakir: Saying: Go early to your tilth if you would cut (the produce).
22.muhammad_sarwar: "Go early to your farms, if you want to pluck the fruits".
22.mohsin_khan: Saying: "Go to your tilth in the morning, if you would pluck the fruits."
22.arberry: 'Come forth betimes upon your tillage, if you would pluck!'

23.sahih_international: So they set out, while lowering their voices,
23.pickthall: So they went off, saying one unto another in low tones:
23.yusuf_ali: So they departed, conversing in secret low tones, (saying)-
23.shakir: So they went, while they consulted together secretly,
23.muhammad_sarwar: They all left, whispering to one another,
23.mohsin_khan: So they departed, conversing in secret low tones (saying),

24.sahih_international: [Saying], "There will surely not enter it today upon you [any] poor person."
24.pickthall: No needy man shall enter it to-day against you.
24.yusuf_ali: "Let not a single indigent person break in upon you into the (garden) this day."
24.shakir: Saying: No poor man shall enter it today upon you.
24.muhammad_sarwar: "Let no beggar come to the garden".
24.mohsin_khan: No Miskin (poor man) shall enter upon you into it today.
24.arberry: 'No needy man shall enter it today against your will.'

25.sahih_international: And they went early in determination, [assuming themselves] able.
25.pickthall: They went betimes, strong in (this) purpose.
25.yusuf_ali: And they opened the morning, strong in an (unjust) resolve.
25.shakir: And in the morning they went, having the power to prevent.
25.muhammad_sarwar: They were resolved to repel the beggars.
25.mohsin_khan: And they went in the morning with strong intention, thinking that they have power (to prevent the poor taking anything of the fruits therefrom).
25.arberry: And they went forth early, determined upon their purpose.

26.sahih_international: But when they saw it, they said, "Indeed, we are lost;
26.pickthall: But when they saw it, they said: Lo! we are in error!
26.yusuf_ali: But when they saw the (garden), they said: "We have surely lost our way:
26.shakir: But when they saw it, they said: Most surely we have gone astray
26.muhammad_sarwar: When they saw the garden, they said, "Surely we have lost our way.
26.mohsin_khan: But when they saw the (garden), they said: "Verily, we have gone astray,"
26.arberry: But when they saw it, they said, 'Surely we are gone astray;

27.yusuf_ali: "Indeed we are shut out (of the fruits of our labour)!"
27.shakir: Nay! we are made to suffer privation.
27.muhammad_sarwar: (No, we are not lost.) In fact, we have been deprived of everything".
27.mohsin_khan: (Then they said): "Nay! Indeed we are deprived of (the fruits)!"
27.arberry: nay, rather we have been robbed!'

28.sahih_international: The most moderate of them said, "Did I not say to you, 'Why do you not exalt [Allah]?' "
28.pickthall: The best among them said: Said I not unto you: Why glorify ye not (Allah)?
28.yusuf_ali: Said one of them, more just (than the rest): "Did I not say to you, 'Why not glorify (Allah)?'"
28.shakir: The best of them said: Did I not say to you, Why do you not glorify (Allah)?
28.muhammad_sarwar: A reasonable one among them said, "Did I not tell you that you should glorify God?"
28.mohsin_khan: The best among them said: "Did I not tell you: why do you not say: Insha' Allah (If Allah will)."
28.arberry: Said the most moderate of them, 'Did I not say to you, "Why do you not give glory?"'

29.sahih_international: They said, "Exalted is our Lord! Indeed, we were wrongdoers."
29.pickthall: They said: Glorified be our Lord! Lo! we have been wrong-doers.
29.yusuf_ali: They said: "Glory to our Lord! Verily we have been doing wrong!"
29.shakir: They said: Glory be to our Lord, surely we were unjust.
29.muhammad_sarwar: They said, "All glory belongs to God. We have certainly been unjust".
29.mohsin_khan: They said: "Glory to Our Lord! Verily, we have been Zalimun (wrong-doers, etc.)."
29.arberry: They said, 'Glory be to God, our Lord; truly, we were evildoers.'

30.sahih_international: Then they approached one another, blaming each other.
30.pickthall: Then some of them drew near unto others, self-reproaching.
30.yusuf_ali: Then they turned, one against another, in reproach.
30.shakir: Then some of them advanced against others, blaming each other.
30.muhammad_sarwar: Some of them started to blame others.
30.mohsin_khan: Then they turned, one against another, in blaming.
30.arberry: And they advanced one upon another, blaming each other.

31.sahih_international: They said, "O woe to us; indeed we were transgressors.
31.pickthall: They said: Alas for us! In truth we were outrageous.
31.yusuf_ali: They said: "Alas for us! We have indeed transgressed!
31.shakir: Said they: O woe to us! surely we were inordinate:
31.muhammad_sarwar: They said, "Woe to us. We have been arrogant.
31.mohsin_khan: They said: "Woe to us! Verily, we were Taghun (transgressors and disobedient, etc.)
31.arberry: They said, 'Woe, alas for us! Truly, we were insolent.

32.sahih_international: Perhaps our Lord will substitute for us [one] better than it. Indeed, we are toward our Lord desirous."
32.pickthall: It may be that our Lord will give us better than this in place thereof. Lo! we beseech our Lord.
32.yusuf_ali: "It may be that our Lord will give us in exchange a better (garden) than this: for we do turn to Him (in repentance)!"
32.shakir: Maybe, our Lord will give us instead one better than it; surely to our Lord do we make our humble petition.
32.muhammad_sarwar: Perhaps our Lord will replace it with a better garden. We turn in repentance to our Lord".
32.mohsin_khan: We hope that our Lord will give us in exchange a better (garden) than this. Truly, we turn to our Lord (wishing for good that He may forgive our sins, and reward us in the Hereafter)."
32.arberry: It may be that our Lord will give us in exchange a better than it; to our Lord we humbly turn.'

33.sahih_international: Such is the punishment [of this world]. And the punishment of the Hereafter is greater, if they only knew.
33.pickthall: Such was the punishment. And verily the punishment of the Hereafter is greater if they did but know.
33.yusuf_ali: Such is the Punishment (in this life); but greater is the Punishment in the Hereafter,- if only they knew!
33.shakir: Such is the chastisement, and certainly the chastisement of the hereafter is greater, did they but know!
33.muhammad_sarwar: Such is the torment if only they knew that the torment in the life hereafter will certainly be greater.
33.mohsin_khan: Such is the punishment (in this life), but truly, the punishment of the Hereafter is greater, if they but knew.
33.arberry: Such is the chastisement; and the chastisement of the world to come, is assuredly greater, did they but know.

34.sahih_international: Indeed, for the righteous with their Lord are the Gardens of Pleasure.
34.pickthall: Lo! for those who keep from evil are gardens of bliss with their Lord.
34.yusuf_ali: Verily, for the Righteous, are Gardens of Delight, in the Presence of their Lord.
34.shakir: Surely those who guard (against evil) shall have with their Lord gardens of bliss.
34.muhammad_sarwar: The pious ones will receive a beautiful Paradise from their Lord.
34.mohsin_khan: Verily, for the Muttaqun (pious and righteous persons - see V. 2:2) are Gardens of delight (Paradise) with their Lord.
34.arberry: Surely for the godfearing shall be Gardens of Bliss with their Lord.

35.sahih_international: Then will We treat the Muslims like the criminals?
35.pickthall: Shall We then treat those who have surrendered as We treat the guilty?
35.yusuf_ali: Shall We then treat the People of Faith like the People of Sin?
35.shakir: What! shall We then make (that is, treat) those who submit as the guilty?
35.muhammad_sarwar: Shall We treat the Muslims like criminals?
35.mohsin_khan: Shall We then treat the (submitting) Muslims like the Mujrimun (criminals, polytheists and disbelievers, etc.)?
35.arberry: What, shall we make those who have surrendered like to the sinners?

36.sahih_international: What is [the matter] with you? How do you judge?
36.pickthall: What aileth you? How foolishly ye judge!
36.yusuf_ali: What is the matter with you? How judge ye?
36.shakir: What has happened to you? How do you judge?
36.muhammad_sarwar: What is the matter with you? How could you judge this to be so?
36.mohsin_khan: What is the matter with you? How judge you?
36.arberry: What ails you then, how you judge?

37.sahih_international: Or do you have a scripture in which you learn
37.pickthall: Or have ye a scripture wherein ye learn
37.yusuf_ali: Or have ye a book through which ye learn-
37.shakir: Or have you a book wherein you read,
37.muhammad_sarwar: Do you have a book from which you study
37.mohsin_khan: Or have you a Book through which you learn.
37.arberry: Or have you a Book wherein you study?

38.sahih_international: That indeed for you is whatever you choose?
38.pickthall: That ye shall indeed have all that ye choose?
38.yusuf_ali: That ye shall have, through it whatever ye choose?
38.shakir: That you have surely therein what you choose?
38.muhammad_sarwar: that tells you to do whatever you want?
38.mohsin_khan: That you shall have all that you choose?
38.arberry: Surely therein you shall have whatever you choose!

39.sahih_international: Or do you have oaths [binding] upon Us, extending until the Day of Resurrection, that indeed for you is whatever you judge?
39.pickthall: Or have ye a covenant on oath from Us that reacheth to the Day of Judgment, that yours shall be all that ye ordain?
39.yusuf_ali: Or have ye Covenants with Us to oath, reaching to the Day of Judgment, (providing) that ye shall have whatever ye shall demand?
39.shakir: Or have you received from Us an agreement confirmed by an oath extending to the day of resurrection that you shall surely have what you demand?
39.muhammad_sarwar: Do you have a covenant with Us which allows you to do whatever you want until the Day of Judgment?
39.mohsin_khan: Or you have oaths from Us, reaching to the Day of Resurrection that yours will be what you judge.
39.arberry: Or have you oaths from Us, reaching to the Day of Resurrection? Surely you shall have whatever you judge!

40.sahih_international: Ask them which of them, for that [claim], is responsible.
40.pickthall: Ask them (O Muhammad) which of them will vouch for that!
40.yusuf_ali: Ask thou of them, which of them will stand surety for that!
40.shakir: Ask them which of them will vouch for that,
40.muhammad_sarwar: (Muhammad), ask which of them can guarantee that on the Day of Judgment.
40.mohsin_khan: Ask them, which of them will stand surety for that!
40.arberry: Ask them, which of them will guarantee that!

41.sahih_international: Or do they have partners? Then let them bring their partners, if they should be truthful.
41.pickthall: Or have they other gods? Then let them bring their other gods if they are truthful
41.yusuf_ali: Or have they some "Partners" (in Allahhead)? Then let them produce their "partners", if they are truthful!
41.shakir: Or have they associates if they are truthful.
41.muhammad_sarwar: they will receive the same thing that the Muslims will? Do they have any witness to such an agreement? Let them bring out such witness, if they are truthful.
41.mohsin_khan: Or have they "partners"? Then let them bring their "partners" if they are truthful!
41.arberry: Or do they have associates? Then let them bring their associates, if they speak truly.

42.sahih_international: The Day the shin will be uncovered and they are invited to prostration but the disbelievers will not be able,
42.pickthall: On the day when it befalleth in earnest, and they are ordered to prostrate themselves but are not able,
42.yusuf_ali: The Day that the shin shall be laid bare, and they shall be summoned to bow in adoration, but they shall not be able,-
42.shakir: On the day when there shall be a severe affliction, and they shall be called upon to make obeisance, but they shall not be able,
42.muhammad_sarwar: On the day when the terrible torment approaches, they will be told (in a mocking way) to prostrate themselves, but they will not be able to do it.
42.mohsin_khan: (Remember) the Day when the Shin shall be laid bare (i.e. the Day of Resurrection) and they shall be called to prostrate (to Allah), but they (hypocrites) shall not be able to do so,
42.arberry: Upon the day when the leg shall be bared, and they shall be summoned to bow themselves, but they cannot;

43.sahih_international: Their eyes humbled, humiliation will cover them. And they used to be invited to prostration while they were sound.
43.pickthall: With eyes downcast, abasement stupefying them. And they had been summoned to prostrate themselves while they were yet unhurt.
43.yusuf_ali: Their eyes will be cast down,- ignominy will cover them; seeing that they had been summoned aforetime to bow in adoration, while they were whole, (and had refused).
43.shakir: Their looks cast down, abasement shall overtake them; and they were called upon to make obeisance indeed while yet they were safe.
43.muhammad_sarwar: Their eyes will be lowered and disgrace will cover them. They had certainly been told to prostrate themselves before God when they were safe and sound.
43.mohsin_khan: Their eyes will be cast down, ignominy will cover them; they used to be called to prostrate (offer prayers), while they were healthy and good (in the life of the world, but they did not).
43.arberry: humbled shall be their eyes, and abasement shall overspread them, for they had been summoned to bow themselves while they were whole.

44.sahih_international: So leave Me, [O Muhammad], with [the matter of] whoever denies the Qur'an. We will progressively lead them [to punishment] from where they do not know.
44.pickthall: Leave Me (to deal) with those who give the lie to this pronouncement. We shall lead them on by steps from whence they know not.
44.yusuf_ali: Then leave Me alone with such as reject this Message: by degrees shall We punish them from directions they perceive not.
44.shakir: So leave Me and him who rejects this announcement; We will overtake them by degrees, from whence they perceive not:
44.muhammad_sarwar: Leave those who reject the Quran to Me and I shall lead them step by step to destruction, without their being aware of it.
44.mohsin_khan: Then leave Me Alone with such as belie this Quran. We shall punish them gradually from directions they perceive not.
44.arberry: So leave Me with him who cries lies to this discourse! We will draw them on little by little whence they know not;

45.sahih_international: And I will give them time. Indeed, My plan is firm.
45.pickthall: Yet I bear with them, for lo! My scheme is firm.
45.yusuf_ali: A (long) respite will I grant them: truly powerful is My Plan.
45.shakir: And I do bear with them, surely My plan is firm.
45.muhammad_sarwar: I shall give them respite, however, My plan is so strong that they will never be able to escape from it.
45.mohsin_khan: And I will grant them a respite. Verily, My Plan is strong.
45.arberry: and I shall respite them -- assuredly My guile is sure.

46.sahih_international: Or do you ask of them a payment, so they are by debt burdened down?
46.pickthall: Or dost thou (Muhammad) ask a fee from them so that they are heavily taxed?
46.yusuf_ali: Or is it that thou dost ask them for a reward, so that they are burdened with a load of debt?-
46.shakir: Or do you ask from them a reward, so that they are burdened with debt?
46.muhammad_sarwar: (Muhammad), do you ask for your preaching any recompense which is too heavy a price for them to pay?
46.mohsin_khan: Or is it that you (O Muhammad SAW) ask them a wage, so that they are heavily burdened with debt?
46.arberry: Or askest thou them for a wage, and so they are weighed down with debt?

47.sahih_international: Or have they [knowledge of] the unseen, so they write [it] down?
47.pickthall: Or is the Unseen theirs that they can write (thereof)?
47.yusuf_ali: Or that the Unseen is in their hands, so that they can write it down?
47.shakir: Or have they (the knowledge of) the unseen, so that they write (it) down?
47.muhammad_sarwar: Do they possess the knowledge of the unseen which confirms the truthfulness of their belief?
47.mohsin_khan: Or that the Ghaib (unseen here in this Verse it means Al-Lauh Al-Mahfuz) is in their hands, so that they can write it down?
47.arberry: Or is the Unseen in their keeping, and so they are writing it down?

48.sahih_international: Then be patient for the decision of your Lord, [O Muhammad], and be not like the companion of the fish when he called out while he was distressed.
48.pickthall: But wait thou for thy Lord's decree, and be not like him of the fish, who cried out in despair.
48.yusuf_ali: So wait with patience for the Command of thy Lord, and be not like the Companion of the Fish,- when he cried out in agony.
48.shakir: So wait patiently for the judgment of your Lord, and be not like the companion of the fish, when he cried while he was in distress.
48.muhammad_sarwar: Exercise patience until the promise of your Lord (to punish the unbelievers) comes true. Do not be like Jonah (who left his people without the permission of God; he wanted them to be punished immediately),
48.mohsin_khan: So wait with patience for the Decision of your Lord, and be not like the Companion of the Fish, when he cried out (to Us) while he was in deep sorrow. (See the Quran, Verse 21:87).
48.arberry: So be thou patient under the judgment of thy Lord, and be not as the Man of the Fish, when he called, choking inwardly.

49.sahih_international: If not that a favor from his Lord overtook him, he would have been thrown onto the naked shore while he was censured.
49.pickthall: Had it not been that favour from his Lord had reached him he surely had been cast into the wilderness while he was reprobate.
49.yusuf_ali: Had not Grace from his Lord reached him, he would indeed have been cast off on the naked shore, in disgrace.
49.shakir: Were it not that favor from his Lord had overtaken him, he would certainly have been cast down upon the naked Found while he was blamed.
49.muhammad_sarwar: and who cried (for help) to his Lord, while imprisoned and helpless inside the fish. Had it not been for a favor from his Lord, he would have been left out in the open, deserving blame for his shortcomings.
49.mohsin_khan: Had not a Grace from his Lord reached him, he would indeed have been (left in the stomach of the fish, but We forgave him), so he was cast off on the naked shore, while he was to be blamed.
49.arberry: Had there not overtaken him a blessing from his Lord he would have been cast upon the wilderness, being condemned.

50.sahih_international: And his Lord chose him and made him of the righteous.
50.pickthall: But his Lord chose him and placed him among the righteous.
50.yusuf_ali: Thus did his Lord choose him and make him of the Company of the Righteous.
50.shakir: Then his Lord chose him, and He made him of the good.
50.muhammad_sarwar: But his Lord chose him as His Prophet and made him one of the righteous ones.
50.mohsin_khan: But his Lord chose him and made him of the righteous.
50.arberry: But his Lord had chosen him, and He placed him among the righteous.

51.sahih_international: And indeed, those who disbelieve would almost make you slip with their eyes when they hear the message, and they say, "Indeed, he is mad."
51.pickthall: And lo! those who disbelieve would fain disconcert thee with their eyes when they hear the Reminder, and they say: Lo! he is indeed mad;
51.yusuf_ali: And the Unbelievers would almost trip thee up with their eyes when they hear the Message; and they say: "Surely he is possessed!"
51.shakir: And those who disbelieve would almost smite you with their eyes when they hear the reminder, and they say: Most surely he is mad.
51.muhammad_sarwar: When the disbelievers listen to you reciting the Quran they almost try to destroy you with their piercing eyes. Then they say, "He is certainly insane".
51.mohsin_khan: And verily, those who disbelieve would almost make you slip with their eyes through hatredness when they hear the Reminder (the Quran), and they say: "Verily, he (Muhammad SAW) is a madman!"
51.arberry: The unbelievers wellnigh strike thee down with their glances, when they hear the Reminder, and they say, 'Surely he is a man possessed!'

52.sahih_international: But it is not except a reminder to the worlds.
52.pickthall: When it is naught else than a Reminder to creation.
52.yusuf_ali: But it is nothing less than a Message to all the worlds.
52.shakir: And it is naught but a reminder to the nations.
52.muhammad_sarwar: The Quran is nothing but a reminder from God to mankind.
52.mohsin_khan: But it is nothing else than a Reminder to all the 'Alamin (mankind, jinns and all that exists).
52.arberry: And it is nothing but a Reminder unto all beings.
